newsitem.title: USA: Cygnus loses claim in Sanofi FemPatch case.
newsitem.headline: Cygnus loses claim in Sanofi FemPatch case.

text.p: The Tribunal of the International Chamber of Commerce has ruled in favor of Sanofi and against Cygnus Inc in a dispute over Cygnus's FemPatch product, Cygnus said Wednesday.
Cygnus said it could be materially and adversely affected by the Tribunal's decision in the final stage of arbitration, when the Tribunal to determine the remedy awarded to Sanofi.
Cygnus had alleged that Sanofi breached a contract by failing to commercialize FemPatch.

According to Cygnus, the arbitration proceedings were initiated by Sanofi in July 1994, with Sanofi alleging that Cygnus breached a contract with Sanofi by entering into a product development agreement with another company for the development of transdermal systems for hormone replacement therapy.
FemPatch, which Cygnus co-developed with a unit of Warner-Lambert Co, is a low-dose transdermal estrogen patch for the treatment of menopausal symptoms.

In a previous stage of the arbitration process, announced in November 1996, the Tribunal found that two transdermal products for hormone replacement therapy licensed by Cygnus to another company fell within the scope of the exclusive license previously granted to Sanofi.

In the initial request for arbitration, Sanofi sought to recover a sum of at least $10 million, royalties on Cygnus's future transdermal systems for the hormone replacement market, amounts for lost market share and profits, together with the costs of the arbitration.

Cygnus had asserted counterclaims for the loss of royalties for the delay and/or refusal to commercialize FemPatch in the United States and the rest of the world, for fees due under the agreement that were not paid, for lost profits from sales in the United States and Canada, and for the loss of valuable market share.
